en.title: The Book of De · Chapter Forty-two · The Way of Heaven
en.原文:
天之道
酉張弓也
高者印之
下者舉之
有餘者𢿃之
不足者補之

故天之道
□云有余而益不足
人之道
云不足而奉又余

孰能有餘而有以取奉於天者
唯又道者乎

是以𦔻人為而弗又
成功而弗居也若此
亓不欲見賢也
en.字龕:
### 益 *yì* ／ 補 *bǔ* ／ 損 *sǔn* — giving ／ mending ／ taking （複合龕 · compound niche）

**字 Graph** ｜ 篆 ![益之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E7%9B%8A.svg) ![補之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E8%A3%9C.svg) ![損之篆](/book-assets/hosuke-laozi-en/zhuan/%E6%90%8D.svg)

**文 Gloss** ｜ The *Shuowen*: 「益，饒也。從水、皿。皿，益之意也。」 — "Abundance. From 水, water, above 皿, a dish — water over the brim of the dish: that is the picture of 益." 「補，完衣也。」 — "To make a garment whole again: mending." 「損，減也。」 — "To lessen." The silk text does not write 損 itself: manuscript A has 𢿃 and manuscript B 云, both read as 損.

**像 Image** ｜ Water over the rim: that is 益 — having so much it spills. A torn robe sewn whole: that is 補 — just enough, no more. Heaven draws the bow: it skims the spill and pours it into the tear.

**義 Sense** ｜ The silk text says Heaven 益s the wanting — gives until they brim; the Wang Bi recension says 補s them — mends them to just-enough. As the commentary reads it: the brimming gift is the heart of Heaven, generous without limit; the mend is only the patching of holes. One graph apart, and Heaven's largesse shrinks to a tailor's shop.
en.對校:
天之道，其猶張弓與？高者抑之，下者舉之；有餘者損之，不足者補之。天之道，損有餘而補不足。
人之道則不然，
:
損不足以奉有餘。
孰能有餘以奉天下？唯有道者。
是以聖人為而不恃，功成而不處，其不欲見賢。
:
en.校記:
Manuscript A (MS A) is damaged at both ends of this chapter: the first two lines, 人之道, 云不足而奉又余 and everything from 唯又道者乎 on follow Manuscript B (MS B); □云有余而益不足 is damaged in both and follows the graphs MS B preserves; the rest follows MS A. Graphs are those outside the brackets in the *Changsha Mawangdui Han mu jianbo jicheng* (2014; hereafter *Jicheng*).

- 天之道: Follows MS B. MS A reads 天下□□; the original editors noted that no other text has 下 here and that it is an interpolated graph, and the *Jicheng* marks it as such: 天{下}【之道】. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 38, n. 195)
- 酉張弓也: Follows MS B; 酉 is read as 猶 "like". MS A reads □□□者也, with 者 before 也. Wang Bi reads 其猶張弓與.
- 高者印之 / 下者舉之: Follows MS A; both manuscripts agree. 印 is read as 抑 "to press down", which is what Wang Bi writes.
- 有餘者𢿃之: Follows MS A. MS A's 𢿃 (員 with 攵), read as 損 "to take from", occurs three times in this chapter (it has sometimes been transcribed as 敗, which drops the 口 and gives a different graph). MS B reads 有余者云之, with 余 read as 餘 and 云 also read as 損. Wang Bi reads 有餘者損之.
- 不足者補之: Follows MS A; in MS B 補 is lost.
- 故天之道: Follows MS A; in MS B all four graphs are lost. Wang Bi lacks 故.
- □云有余而益不足: Damaged in both manuscripts; it follows MS B, which preserves more, though its first graph is lost. MS A reads 𢿃有□□□□□. Before 不足 the 1980 edition restored 補 after the received texts; the *Jicheng* replaces it with □, since MS B has 益 here and the Peking University manuscript 奉, and what MS A wrote cannot be determined. Wang Bi reads 損有餘而補不足. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 38, n. 196)
- 人之道: Follows MS B; lost in MS A. Wang Bi reads 人之道則不然.
- 云不足而奉又余: Follows MS B; 云 is read as 損, and 又余 as 有餘. MS A reads □不然𢿃□□□奉有餘, with 不然 "not so", as in Wang Bi; its 然 is written in a corrupt form. Wang Bi reads 損不足以奉有餘.
- 孰能有餘而有以取奉於天者: Follows MS A, which also has a final 乎. MS B reads 夫孰能又余而□□奉於天者, opening with 夫. The two lost graphs after 而 were restored in 1980 as 有以; Gao Ming judged that this does not fit the sense, and the *Jicheng*, following the Peking University manuscript, restores 有（又）取 instead. Wang Bi reads 孰能有餘以奉天下. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 38, n. 197; p. 204, n. 145)
- 唯又道者乎: Follows MS B; 又 is read as 有. In MS A this line is lost. The 1980 edition restored it from MS B as 唯有道者乎; the *Jicheng*, following the Peking University manuscript, restores 唯有道者也. Wang Bi reads 唯有道者. (*Jicheng* IV, p. 38, n. 197)
- 是以𦔻人為而弗又 / 成功而弗居也若此: Follows MS B; lost in MS A. Wang Bi reads 是以聖人為而不恃，功成而不處, without 若此 "like this".
- 亓不欲見賢也: Follows MS B; MS A preserves only 見賢也. Wang Bi reads 其不欲見賢.
en.疏:
杳眇曰：

天之道，猶張弓者也。弓之道，在乎正曲直；道之在天下，在乎均高低。觀夫張弓之時，弦高一尺者抑之，低一寸者舉之，有餘者損之，不足者補之，此天道之象也。《周易》謙卦曰「君子以裒多益寡」，益卦取風雷相助之象，聖人觀象取法，治世之要，其在斯乎。

天之道，損有餘而益不足，是乃均平之義，非特填補之謂也。《說文》云「益，饒也」，「補，完衣也」。益者增益之，使其有餘而溥博；補者填缺之，使其僅足而已。天心之溥博如是，則萬物各安其分，而不至於偏枯。人之道則不然，損不足而奉有餘，是趨於偏，去天愈遠矣。

考之帛書，與王弼本之可言者三。其一，帛書甲本首作「天下□□」，乙本作「天之道」，與王弼同。原注謂各本皆無「下」字，此「下」乃衍文，《集成》從之；然則甲本亦當讀作「天之道」，與下文「故天之道」「人之道」相對，天人之分乃明。其二，帛書乙本作「益不足」（甲本此字殘，北大本作「奉」），王弼本作「補不足」，「益」之與「補」，義有淺深之別。其三，帛書作「取奉於天者」，王弼本作「奉天下」。取奉於天者，聖人斂其有餘而還之天，不敢自私之意也。

夫聖人為而弗有，成功而弗居，不欲見賢，三者一貫，皆上德无為之旨爾。得失無動於心，功遂身退而德不輟，自伐自矜則有道者不處。弓之所以能中者，以其不恃其滿；道之所以能久者，以其不居其功。聖人知「有之以為利，无之以為用」，是以退身而功存，外生而德溥。世人祇知取之為利，不知舍之為用，其去聖人遠矣。
en.疏英:
Yaomiao says:

The Way of Heaven is like the drawing of a bow. The bow's way is to set crooked and straight aright; the Dao's way in the world is to even high and low. Watch the bow drawn: the limb an inch too high is pressed down; the limb an inch too low is raised; the surplus is taken from; the wanting is made good — the image of the Way of Heaven. The Changes says of the hexagram Qian ䷎ (Modesty), "the noble man takes from the much to give to the little," and of Yi ䷩ (Increase), wind and thunder aiding each other. The sage watches the images and takes his law from them — the crux of ordering the world lies here.

The Way of Heaven takes from the surplus to give to the wanting: this is the sense of evening out, not merely of patching. The *Shuowen*: "益 is to brim over"; "補 is to make a garment whole." 益 adds until there is bounty and breadth; 補 fills the gap to just-enough. Heaven's heart is broad like the brimming gift, so the ten thousand things each rest in their allotments and nothing withers at the edge. The way of man is otherwise: taking from the wanting to offer to the surplus — tilting toward the lopsided, ever farther from Heaven.

Collating the silk text against Wang Bi, three points. First, silk manuscript A opens 天下□□, where manuscript B, like Wang Bi, has 天之道. The first editors note that no other text has 下 and judge it an intrusion, and the *Jicheng* agrees; manuscript A, then, also reads "the Way of Heaven," set against "the Way of Heaven" and "the way of man" below, and the line between Heaven and man comes clear. Second, silk manuscript B has 益不足 (A's graph is lost; the Peking University slips have 奉), "giving to the wanting," for Wang Bi's 補不足, "patching the wanting" — 益 and 補 differ in depth, as the niche above shows. Third, the silk text has 取奉於天者, "taking to offer up to Heaven," for Wang Bi's 奉天下, "offering to all-under-heaven": the sage gathers in his surplus and returns it to Heaven, never daring to hold it privately.

The sage works and does not possess; completes the work and does not dwell in it; has no wish to be seen as worthy — three clauses, one thread, all of the highest De's non-doing. Gain and loss do not move the heart: the work done, the body withdraws, and the De does not cease; self-boasting and self-flaunting have no place in the man of the Dao. The bow hits because it does not lean on its full draw; the Dao lasts because it does not dwell in its merit. The sage knows "presence gives the advantage, absence gives the use" — so he steps back and the work endures, sets himself aside and his De spreads wide. The world knows only that taking is profit; it does not know that letting go is use — far from the sage indeed.
en.英譯:
The Way of Heaven is like the drawing of a bow: what is high it presses down; what is low it raises up; what has surplus it takes from; what falls short it makes good (補).

Thus the Way of Heaven takes from the surplus to give (益) to the wanting; the way of man takes from the wanting to offer to the surplus.

Who can have surplus, and take it to offer up to Heaven? Only one who has the Dao.

Hence the sage works and does not possess; completes the work and does not dwell in it — he has no wish to be seen as worthy.

帛書甲乙.甲: 天下□□□□□者也高者印之∠下者舉之有餘者𢿃之∠不足者補之‧故天之道𢿃有□□□□□□□□□不然𢿃□□□奉有餘孰能有餘而有以取奉於天者乎□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□見賢也

校記:
本章甲本首尾皆殘：首二句、「人之道」「云不足而奉又余」及「唯又道者乎」以下據乙本，「□云有余而益不足」二本皆殘而據乙本存字，餘據甲本；字從《集成》（2014）括號外原字。

- 天之道：據乙本。甲本作「天下□□」，原注謂各本皆無「下」字，此「下」是衍文；《集成》加衍文號，作「天{下}【之道】」。（《集成》肆·頁38·注195）
- 酉張弓也：據乙本，「酉」讀為「猶」。甲本作「□□□者也」，「也」上有「者」字。王弼本作「其猶張弓與」。
- 高者印之　下者舉之：從甲本，甲乙同；「印」讀為「抑」，王弼本作「抑」。
- 有餘者𢿃之：從甲本。甲本「𢿃」字从員从攵，讀為「損」，本章三見（舊或錄作「敗」，失其「口」，別為一字）；乙本作「有余者云之」，「余」讀為「餘」，「云」亦讀為「損」。王弼本作「有餘者損之」。
- 不足者補之：從甲本；乙本「補」字殘。
- 故天之道：從甲本；乙本此四字殘。王弼本無「故」。
- □云有余而益不足：二本皆殘，乙本存字多，據之；乙本首字殘。甲本作「𢿃有□□□□□」，「不足」上一字殘，原釋文據傳本補「補」，《集成》改作「□」：此字乙本作「益」，北大本作「奉」，甲本原作何字不能定。王弼本作「損有餘而補不足」。（《集成》肆·頁38·注196）
- 人之道：據乙本；甲本殘去。王弼本作「人之道則不然」。
- 云不足而奉又余：據乙本，「云」讀為「損」，「又余」讀為「有餘」。甲本作「□不然𢿃□□□奉有餘」，有「不然」二字，與王弼本合；其「然」字原作譌體。王弼本作「損不足以奉有餘」。
- 孰能有餘而有以取奉於天者：從甲本，甲本句末尚有「乎」字。乙本作「夫孰能又余而□□奉於天者」，句首多「夫」；「而」下二字殘，原釋文補「有以」，高明以為不合文義，《集成》從北大本改補「有（又）取」。王弼本作「孰能有餘以奉天下」。（《集成》肆·頁38·注197；頁204·注145）
- 唯又道者乎：據乙本，「又」讀為「有」。甲本此句殘去，原釋文據乙本補作「唯有道者乎」，《集成》依北大本改補作「唯有道者也」。王弼本作「唯有道者」。（《集成》肆·頁38·注197）
- 是以𦔻人為而弗又　成功而弗居也若此：據乙本；甲本殘去。王弼本作「是以聖人為而不恃，功成而不處」，無「若此」。
- 亓不欲見賢也：據乙本；甲本唯存「見賢也」三字。王弼本作「其不欲見賢」。

天之道，其猶張弓與？高者抑之，下者舉之；有餘者損之，不足者補之。天之道，損有餘而補不足。

是以聖人為而不恃，功成而不處，其不欲見賢。
